title: Supreme Court Staggered Term Limits & Judicial Reform
rootClaim: Imposing 18-year staggered term limits on U.S. Supreme Court Justices is essential to restore democratic legitimacy and depoliticize judicial appointments.

branches.text: Depoliticization & Democratic Regularity: Staggered term limits eliminate strategic retirement timing, regularize vacancies, and align court jurisprudence with democratically elected administrations over time.

children.text: Elimination of Strategic Resignations: Life tenure incentivizes justices to delay retirement until ideological allies hold the presidency, turning judicial departures into partisan political maneuvers.
Article III Good Behavior Barrier: Article III guarantees justices hold office 'during good Behavior', meaning term limits would require a constitutional amendment rather than standard legislation.

Senior Status Statutory Architecture: Statutes can transition justices to lower circuit duty or senior advisory status after 18 years, preserving Article III judicial commission while rotating main bench dockets.

Regularization of Confirmation Battles: Establishing two guaranteed judicial appointments per four-year presidential term de-escalates the high-stakes, apocalyptic nature of random confirmation fights.
Post-Court Conflict of Interest: Justices concluding 18-year terms in middle age may craft rulings to curry favor with future corporate, academic, or political employers.

branches.text: Protection of Judicial Independence & Legal Stability: Life tenure insulates the judiciary from majoritarian political headwinds and ensures constitutional continuity.

children.text: Insulation from Democratic Pressure: Life tenure empowers judges to issue essential but unpopular constitutional rulings without fear of electoral retaliation or job loss.
Counter-Majoritarian Drag: Decades-long tenure can entrench an out-of-touch, non-representative judicial supermajority that overrides democratic legislative will indefinitely.
Jurisprudential Stare Decisis: Frequent regular rotation of justices risks hyper-volatile swings in constitutional precedent every presidential election cycle.

definitions.description: A system where judges serve fixed, offset terms (e.g., 18 years) so that vacancies occur at predictable, regular intervals.
A federal judicial status where semi-retired judges continue performing light judicial duties while making way for new full-time appointees.
The provision in the U.S. Constitution specifying that federal judges hold their offices during 'good Behavior' (effectively life tenure unless impeached).
The legal principle of determining points in litigation according to precedent set by prior judicial decisions.
